checkpoints.title: Core particles
checkpoints.subtitle: は, が, か, に, で, and more

points.pattern: ちゃいけない・じゃいけない
points.blurb: Japanese has several ways to tell someone they shouldn't do something — from a parent scolding a child to a formal workplace rule. This lesson covers the casual, spoken end: the kind you'd hear from a friend, a parent, or in everyday conversation. You'll recognize it when someone sets a boundary and know when to say "you shouldn't" versus "you must not."
points.structure:
Take the verb's て-form and drop て. Add ちゃ or じゃ, then いけない or ダメ.

たべる → たべて → たべちゃ + いけない

If the て-form ends in で, use じゃ instead of ちゃ.

のむ → のんで → のんじゃ + いけない

formation.body:
Take the verb's negative stem (ない-form without ない) and add ちゃ or きゃ.

いく → いかない → いかなくちゃ
formation.title: From the negative ない-stem

formation.body: なくちゃ and なきゃ often stand alone as "gotta / have to." You can add いけない for emphasis.
formation.title: Short forms

usage.body: Spoken shorthand for なければならない. Used with friends and family.
usage.title: Casual obligation

usage.body: Same obligation meaning, but なくちゃ is informal. Avoid in formal writing.
usage.title: Compared to なければならない

points.blurb: Japanese doesn't bolt -est onto adjectives the way English does — it leans on one word that means 'number one.' Drop いちばん in front of almost any adjective or verb phrase and you instantly have a superlative. You'll hear it everywhere from menu descriptions to sports commentary, and once you've got it, you can rank anything.
points.structure:
Place いちばん directly before the adjective.

この店がいちばん安い。
This shop is the cheapest.

Same pattern — いちばん comes before the adjective.

彼女がいちばん元気だ。
She is the most energetic.

Add の中で before いちばん to say 'the most among ~.'

クラスの中でいちばん背が高い。
The tallest in the class.

points.title: が①
points.shortDefinition: subject marker; who or what acts
points.headlineEnglish: subject marker; identifies who or what acts
points.blurb: Marks the doer — who or what performs the action. Often answers 誰が or 何が.
points.structure:
Noun + が + predicate

星が見える。
You can see stars.

formation.title: Noun + が
formation.body:
Attach が to the noun that performs the verb.

兄が来た。
My older brother came.

formation.title: Answering 誰が・何が
formation.body:
Questions with 誰が or 何が take が in the answer.

誰が来た？ → 友達が来た。

usage.title: New information
usage.body: Use が when you identify someone or something for the first time. Once they're on the table, は often takes over.

examples.romaji: dare ga kita? ani ga kita.

drills.contrastLabel: Identifying who did it vs. stating a topic

contrastDrills.contrastLabel: Identifying who did it vs. stating a topic

points.title: が②
points.blurb: Between two ideas, が means "but" — a touch more formal than けど.
points.structure:
Clause + が + clause

忙しいが、楽しみだ。
I'm busy, but I'm looking forward to it.

formation.title: Clause + が + clause
formation.body:
Link contrasting ideas with が.

遠いが、行きたい。
It's far, but I want to go.

usage.title: Soft contrast
usage.body: The first part admits a downside; the second part is what you really want to say.

examples.english: I'm busy, but I'm looking forward to it.
It's far, but I want to go.
It's expensive, but I'll buy it.
It's raining, but I'm heading out.

drills.prompt: It's expensive, but I'll buy it.

points.title: か①
points.blurb: Between two nouns, か means "or" — pick one.
points.structure:
A + か + B

ラーメンかうどん？
Ramen or udon?

formation.title: A + か + B
formation.body:
Put か between the options.

赤か青？
Red or blue?

usage.title: Offering a choice
usage.body: Present alternatives and let the listener choose. Often casual — no です needed.

points.title: か②
points.blurb: At the end of a sentence, か turns a statement into a yes/no question.
points.structure:
Statement + か

分かりますか。
Do you understand?

formation.title: Statement + か
formation.body:
Add か to ask yes/no.

行きますか。
Will you go?

formation.title: Polite questions
formation.body:
With です or ます → ですか / ますか.

大丈夫ですか。
Are you okay?

usage.title: Yes/no questions
usage.body: か asks whether something is true. Answer with はい, いいえ, or a fuller reply.

points.title: で①
points.blurb: Marks where an action happens — not where you're headed (that's に).
points.structure:
Place + で + action

図書館で本を読む。
Read a book at the library.

formation.title: Place + で + verb
formation.body:
Attach で to the location of the action.

海で泳ぐ。
Swim at the sea.

usage.title: Stage vs. destination
usage.body: 駅に行く = go to the station. 駅で待つ = wait at the station.

examples.english: Read a book at the library.

points.title: で②
points.blurb: Marks the tool, vehicle, or method — how you do something.
points.structure:
Means + で

ペンで書く。
Write with a pen.

formation.title: Means + で
formation.body:
Put で after the tool or method.

自転車で来た。
I came by bicycle.

usage.title: How or with what
usage.body: Answers "by what means?" — bus, chopsticks, Japanese, email.

examples.english: Hold it in your left hand.
After watching the movie, I'll go home.
examples.japanese: 映画を見てから、帰ります。

points.shortDefinition: is okay; is it alright to, can I do ___
points.blurb: Use this when asking if yourself (the speaker) can do something. Like entering a store; can I enter? Or asking to take pictures at a musuem; can I take pictures here? The も may be omitted in casual speech, while the いい may be swapped with よろしい to fit a more formal / respectful tone.
points.structure:
Take the verb's て-form and drop て. 

たべる → たべて、はいる→ はいって

いい means good: literally meaning 'good if I do x?'

はいってもいい、食べてもいい、、つかってもいい

points.title: に・へ
points.blurb: Both mark direction toward a place. に is everyday; へ sounds a bit more written or directional.
points.structure:
Place + に / へ + go/head

空港へ向かう。
Head for the airport.

formation.title: Movement toward
formation.body:
Either particle works with 行く, 向かう, 進む.

北に進む。 / 北へ進む。

usage.title: に vs. へ
usage.body: For most destinations they're interchangeable with 行く. へ emphasizes "toward" — common on signs and in writing.

points.title: に
points.blurb: Pins a time, destination, or target — when, where to, or to whom.
points.structure:
Time/place/person + に

三時に会う。
Meet at three o'clock.

formation.title: Destination
formation.body:
Place + に + movement verb

医者に行く。
Go to the doctor.

formation.title: Time
formation.body:
Clock time + に

毎朝六時に起きる。
Wake up at six every morning.

formation.title: Target
formation.body:
Person + に + give/say/call

彼に借りる。
Borrow from him.

usage.title: に vs. で
usage.body: に = destination or point in time. で = where an action happens (レストランで食べる).

points.headlineEnglish: because of; the reason is that
points.title: ので
は
points.blurb: Marks what you're talking about — the topic. Think "As for X…" and then say something about it.
points.structure:
Noun + は + comment

東京は人が多い。
Tokyo has a lot of people.

formation.title: Noun + は
formation.body:
Place は after the word you want to talk about.

お昼はパンを食べる。
For lunch, I eat bread.

usage.title: Topic, not subject
usage.body: は frames the sentence. What follows describes that topic — not always the doer of an action.

usage.title: Compared to が
usage.body: が spotlights who acts (猫が来た). は keeps talking about something already on the table (猫は小さい).

points.title: も
points.blurb: Adds "also" or "too" — includes something in what was already mentioned.
points.structure:
Noun + も

田中さんも来る。
Tanaka is coming too.

formation.title: Noun + も
formation.body:
Swap は or が for も to add "also."

犬も好き。
I like dogs too.

usage.title: Adding to the set
usage.body: も layers on: 猫が好き。犬も好き。 = I like cats. I like dogs too.
